```{r}
by_country <- socviz::organdata |>
  group_by(consent_law, country) |>
  summarize(
    donors_mean = mean(donors, na.rm = TRUE),
    donors_sd = sd(donors, na.rm = TRUE),
    gdp_mean = mean(gdp, na.rm = TRUE),
    health_mean = mean(health, na.rm = TRUE),
    roads_mean = mean(roads, na.rm = TRUE),
    cerebvas_mean = mean(cerebvas, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```


```{r}
by_country <- socviz::organdata |>
  group_by(consent_law, country) |>
  summarize_if(is.numeric, lst(mean, sd), na.rm = TRUE) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
p <- ggplot(
  data = by_country,
  mapping = aes(x = roads_mean, 
                y = donors_mean)
)

p +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(aes(label = country))
```
```{r}
p +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = country),
    hjust = 0,
    size = 3.5,
    nudge_x = 0.05, # Using the same 
                    # unit on the 
                    # x-axis scale
    check_overlap = TRUE
  )
```

```{r}
ev <- read_csv("https://bcdanl.github.io/data/electric_vehicles_WA.csv")

ev |> 
  paged_table()
```

```{r}
# Question 1 
#Create summary datasets:

#Top 10 counties by number of EVs
#Top 10 makes by number of EVs
#Average electric range for makes with at least 500 vehicles
library(tidyverse)
library(ggthemes)
library(rmarkdown)

top10_countries <- ev |>
  count(county) |>
  slice_max(n, n =10,
            with_ties = T)

```

```{r}
top10_makers <- ev |>
  count(make) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 10,
            with_ties = T)
```
 
```{r}
avg_eletric_range <- ev |>
  group_by(make) |>
  summarize(n = n(),
            electric_range_mean = mean(electric_range, na.rm = T), 
            electric_range_mean = round(electric_range_mean, 2)) |>
        
  
```
 
```{r}
avg_eletric_range
```

# Question 5
```{r}
# Using the range_by_make scatterplot, add a custom annotation with annotate() that points out the make with the highest average electric range.

# Tasks
# Add a short text note such as "Highest average range"
# Place the annotation near the relevant point
# Also, add a segment or arrow.

```

```{r}
top10_countries|>
  mutate(
    country = fct_reorder(country, n)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x=n,
             y = country,
             fill = country)) +
  geom_col() +
  gemo_text(aes(label = scales::comma(n) ),
            hjust=0,
            nudge_x= 1000
            )+
  scale_fill_fivethirtyeight() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, max(top10_countries$n)*1.5)) +
  guides(fill = "none")+
  theme_insum()
```
# Question 6
```{r}
# Use county_counts to create a bar chart with:

# EV counts on the x-axis
# counties on the y-axis
# bars created with geom_col()
# Then add the count values on top of the bars using # geom_text().

# Tasks
# reorder counties by count
# place the numbers slightly above the bars
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(county_count, aes(x = count,
                          y = reorder(county, count))) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = count),
            hjust = -0.2) +
  labs(
    x = "EV Counts",
    y = "County",
    title = "EV Counts by County"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
